paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God doesn't want a building to be proud of. He wants a people who live what they say. The crowd at the gate kept chanting, 'This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD,' and God called those "deceptive words" (Jeremiah 7:4). Walking through the right doors didn't change the way they treated people.

God spelled out what the real thing looks like: act justly toward one another, stop oppressing the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, and quit following other gods (Jeremiah 7:5-6). They were doing the opposite, then standing in His house and saying, 'We are delivered' (Jeremiah 7:10). I think that hits close to home for all of us. It's easy to lean on church words, church habits and a church address, and call that being right with God. A gym membership never lifted a single weight, and showing up never made anybody ready.

But hear the good news tucked inside the warning. God says, "Correct your ways and deeds, and I will let you live in this place" (Jeremiah 7:3). He spoke again and again and called to them (Jeremiah 7:13), because He wanted them to turn back. So today, baker, don't just show up. Let what you learn in the Word reach your hands, your words and the way you treat the people nobody else notices. And this story isn't over, because the LORD has more to say.
